title: A/B experimentation framework for batching & KV-cache configuration
creator: Owen Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's adaptive batching and KV cache heuristics are a major lever for reducing per-token cost, but we lack a repeatable, low-risk A/B testing framework to evaluate candidate batching/caching configurations across real traffic. Current manual experiments have inconsistent metrics, limited cohort isolation, and no automated rollback gating on customer-facing signals.

Goal:
Build an experimentation and analysis playbook + dashboards that enable safe A/B tests of batching and KV-cache config changes. Deliverables: 1) cohort assignment & feature-flagging integration, 2) telemetry + aggregated metrics set, 3) Grafana dashboards and BigQuery analysis notebooks, 4) automated guardrail gates with rollback automation.

Success metrics (primary):
- Delta in cost per 1k tokens served (normalized by model + sequence length distribution) - target detectable savings >= 6% for 90% of workloads in experiment.
- No regression in latency P95 beyond 10% relative to baseline for the test cohort.
- No customer-facing error rate increase > 0.2 percentage points.
- Model output quality (see quality metrics below) has no statistically significant degradation at alpha=0.05 across sampled prompts.

Secondary metrics:
- Throughput (rps) improvement, batch size distribution shift, cache hit rate, GPU utilization, queueing time.

Experiment design:
- Cohorts: random traffic split at request-level using feature flag service (stable ID hashing based on account+route). Cohorts: Control (baseline config), Variant A (aggressive batching), Variant B (aggressive KV cache TTL + prefix reuse). Typical split 60/20/20 to prioritize stability.
- Units of randomization: customer_id for enterprise-affecting features; request-level for anonymous low-risk traffic.
- Duration: minimum 7 days or until minimum sample size reached (see sample size). For short-lived endpoints we extend window to capture tail percentiles.
- Sample size / power: use baseline variance from last 30 days; target 80% power to detect 6% reduction in cost-per-token. Default sample sizing script in BigQuery to be used before rollout.
- Statistical tests: permutation test for cost metrics (non-normal), bootstrap for P95 latency CI, Benjamini-Hochberg for multiple endpoints. Documented notebook will produce p-values and effect sizes.

Safety & rollback gating:
- Automated gates evaluated in real-time in the dashboard with 5-min buckets and 1-hour rolling windows. If any of the following triggers, the rollback automation will flip the feature flag and notify on-call:
  - Latency P95 increases > 20% for two consecutive 1-hour windows AND error rate increase > 0.1pp.
  - Error rate increase > 0.5pp for any 10-minute bucket.
  - Customer-impacting alerts (SLO breach) fired for the affected model/route.
- Manual rollback: runbooks for SRE/Platform to follow if automation not appropriate (e.g., high-importance customer affected).

Telemetry events to capture:
- batch_config_applied (config_id, variant, cohort, start_ts)
- batch_metrics_bucket (bucket_ts, cohort, model, route, tokens, cost_estimate, batch_count, avg_batch_size)
- cache_hit_sample (cohort, model, key_prefix, hit_bool) sampled 1% of requests for quality/coverage analysis
- cohort_assignment (request_id, cohort, customer_id)
- rollback_action (config_id, reason, triggered_by)

Quality measurement (to guard against silent degradation):
- Use existing eval prompt sets for high-impact routes. For sampled requests, compute embedding similarity between control & variant outputs (cosine similarity) and a small set of logits-based hallucination heuristics.
- Automated A/B quality audit: sample N=200 requests per cohort per day for high-volume routes and run an offline evaluation job. Flag if similarity mean drops below 0.92 or hallucination heuristic increases by 50%.

Dashboards & analysis artifacts:
- Create Grafana dashboards (panels):
  - "Batching A/B Overview" — cost per 1k tokens, cost delta, cohort comparisons, CI bands, sample counts.
  - "Latency & Reliability by Cohort" — P50/P95/P99, error rates, queue time, GPU utilization heatmap.
  - "Cache Coverage & Hit Ratio" — TTL distributions, hit-rate over time, prefix reuse stats.
  - "Quality Signals" — embedding similarity distributions, hallucination heuristic, example diff viewer (linked to S3/Drive).
- BigQuery notebooks: data extraction + permutation test, bootstrap CI scripts, power/sample-size helper. Notebook link: https://drive.redwood.company/docs/abtest-batch-cache-analysis (placeholder).
- Alert panels with thresholds matching rollback gating.

Implementation plan / engineering tasks (high level):
- Instrumentation: add telemetry events and metrics exporters (ENG-8232).
- Feature flag integration: implement cohort assignment hooks and server-side stable hashing (ENG-8205).
- Rollout controller: build automation that monitors signals and flips flags via API (ENG-8250).
- Dashboards & queries: implement Grafana dashboards and BigQuery notebooks (ENG-8235).
- Test harness: synthetic workload generator to simulate variable seq lengths and burstiness for pre-rollout validation (ENG-8240).

Dependencies:
- data-platform: access to aggregated token billing tables and model runtime metrics.
- Observability infra: short retention 1-min granularity in metrics pipeline for 24-48 hours.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive batching may increase P99 tail latency for some long-sequence flows. Mitigation: exclude long-sequence routes from the experiment or add sequence-length aware sampling.
- Risk: quality regressions not captured by heuristics. Mitigation: human-in-the-loop spot checks and conservative rollout percentages for nontrivial model changes.

Notes on uniqueness: This ticket focuses on end-to-end A/B experiment framework and automated rollback gating (not: one-off cost experiments). It pairs cost signals with quality signals and sets concrete statistical testing and automation requirements so experiments can be reproducible and low-risk.
